buildings.name: Meridian Crescent Residences
buildings.purpose: landmark permanent apartments opening toward Long Horizon Park
buildings.exteriorMotif: five rotated brick and ceramic sections with deep inhabited balconies, bronze portals, planted terraces, and a green photovoltaic crown

buildings.name: Helix Terraces
buildings.purpose: family-oriented stepped housing
buildings.exteriorMotif: two curving strands descending from seven to four storeys with planted balcony channels, cylindrical stairs, bridges, and greenhouse roofs

buildings.name: Circadian House
buildings.purpose: quiet accommodation for rotating and nocturnal staff
buildings.exteriorMotif: heavy charcoal ceramic shell, deeply recessed constellation windows, double shutters, acoustic entrance court, and circadian roof band
buildings.lighting: low amber and protected roof phase band

buildings.name: Rootline Garden Homes
buildings.purpose: domestic clusters at the Environmental Science transition
buildings.exteriorMotif: earth-embedded two and three storey clusters, sloping planted roofs, copper vents, rain channels, ponds, and small covered gates

buildings.name: Lattice Twin Residences
buildings.purpose: apartments for single residents, couples, and early-career researchers
buildings.exteriorMotif: two angled eleven-storey towers wrapped in champagne structural lattices with two translucent bridges and open sensor crowns

buildings.name: Parallax Long-Stay Apartments
buildings.purpose: adaptable months-to-years accommodation
buildings.exteriorMotif: three laterally shifted reddish ceramic blocks with bronze glass, movable screens, tree-filled terraces, and a photovoltaic Continuum canopy

buildings.name: Archive Court Residences
buildings.purpose: quiet housing for senior and retired researchers and long-term fellows
buildings.exteriorMotif: four black-brick wings around a narrow court, parabolic bronze arcades, observatory-like copper-capped corner towers, and reflecting channel

buildings.name: Orbit Family Blocks
buildings.purpose: family apartments surrounding a protected park
buildings.exteriorMotif: six rounded polygonal blocks linked by a continuous low canopy, broad screened balconies, uneven green roofs, photovoltaic sails, and ventilation chimneys

buildings.name: Commons Cooperative
buildings.purpose: communal housing for doctoral researchers, technicians, apprentices, and temporary teams
buildings.exteriorMotif: four framed modular wings around a sheltered courtyard with glass bridges and a luminous elevated garden canopy
buildings.lighting: moving silhouettes and diffuse courtyard light

buildings.name: Horizon Accessible Residences
buildings.purpose: universally accessible and adaptable housing
buildings.exteriorMotif: low limestone bars around broad courts with landscape ramps, sheltered docking porches, transparent roof-loop windscreens, and photovoltaic canopies

buildings.name: Resident Commons Hall
buildings.purpose: social and civic center of the residential district
buildings.exteriorMotif: three rotated stone, timber-glass, and translucent volumes above a public planted stair beneath branching bronze roof supports
buildings.placementZone: Continuum gateway and Long Horizon Park

buildings.name: Neighborhood Laboratory House
buildings.purpose: bookable low-risk resident laboratories
buildings.exteriorMotif: three-storey ceramic and brick square around a planted light court with projecting modules, status panels, bronze mesh, greenhouse, and screened service edge
buildings.lighting: cyan green amber and ultraviolet status indicators

buildings.name: Fabrication Mews
buildings.purpose: bookable electronics, repair, fabrication, and artistic-technology workshops
buildings.exteriorMotif: eight narrow workshops facing a covered service court under a folded photovoltaic roof with copper-orange safety edges and a planted acoustic wall

buildings.name: Solstice Covered Pool
buildings.purpose: quiet residential swimming and wellness
buildings.exteriorMotif: low oval timber-rib roof with glass and photovoltaic strips above a rough stone base, water-glimpse band, bronze rain chains, and planted mechanical mounds

buildings.name: Wintergarden Recreation Hall
buildings.purpose: covered garden, exercise, indoor courts, and communal recreation
buildings.exteriorMotif: three asymmetrical glass conservatories on a dark-brick base with climbing cables, shade panels, exercise terrace, ventilation fins, and kinetic weather panels

buildings.name: Resident Loop Mall
buildings.purpose: small nonstop neighborhood mall
buildings.exteriorMotif: two-storey ceramic and bronze ring around a tree-pierced covered court with deep shop recesses, parcel wall, external balcony, and four broad stairs

buildings.name: The Common Table Market Hall
buildings.purpose: principal neighborhood restaurant and food market
buildings.exteriorMotif: long low brick-colonnaded hall beneath a folded zinc roof with glass lanterns, sculptural extraction chimneys, communal tables, and rain-garden bridges
buildings.lighting: warm all-hour counter and cafe light

buildings.name: Nocturne Cafe and Reading Pavilion
buildings.purpose: continuously open quiet cafe and reading place
buildings.exteriorMotif: narrow bronze-glass pavilion on dark stone surrounded by reflecting water, bridges, planting, adjustable shutters, and a sharply projecting timber-lined roof
buildings.lighting: narrow amber soffit and occupancy beacon

buildings.name: Night Clinic and Pharmacy
buildings.purpose: urgent basic care, occupational assessment, telemedicine, pharmacy, and minor treatment
buildings.exteriorMotif: compact pale stone block with silver metal, translucent green glass, deep horizontal frames, medical arrival canopy, planted setback, and screened rear service
buildings.placementZone: visible residential to Ever Hour boundary
buildings.lighting: calm green pharmacy and entrance light

buildings.name: Seedling House
buildings.purpose: childcare, after-school activities, family support, and introductory science education
buildings.exteriorMotif: rounded ceramic, timber, and colored-glass pavilions beneath one undulating photovoltaic roof in a protected observation garden

buildings.name: Ever Hour Exchange Hotel
buildings.purpose: central guest hotel and district landmark
buildings.exteriorMotif: eight-storey basalt-to-opaline crescent around Chronogarden with bronze glazing, moving chronometer fins, collaboration-time crown, and brass-lined oval forecourt
buildings.lighting: warm silver and pale gold with time crown

buildings.name: Meridian Visiting Scholars Hotel
buildings.purpose: high-capacity visiting scholar accommodation beside the laboratory zone
buildings.exteriorMotif: four rotated ceramic and titanium tower sections with deep sample-tray windows above a sheltered public plaza, Bench Street bridge, sensors, and weather beacon

buildings.name: Interim House
buildings.purpose: apartment-style accommodation for several weeks to one year
buildings.exteriorMotif: two shifted six-storey slabs around a planted court with smoked bronze glass, mesh screens, recessed passage, and suspended garden bridges

buildings.name: Null Hour Transit Lodge
buildings.purpose: compact late-arrival and early-departure lodging
buildings.exteriorMotif: black metal rectangle with scattered square windows behind expanded mesh, continuous numbered arcade, cut triangular arrival court, and 00:00 transit sign

buildings.name: Fellows' Cloister Guesthouse
buildings.purpose: guesthouse for senior visitors, lecturers, historians, and artists in residence
buildings.exteriorMotif: three-storey black-brick quadrangle with parabolic arcades, bronze inner walks, planted zinc roofs, engraved copper-capped towers, and long water garden

buildings.name: Scientific Interchange Forum
buildings.purpose: principal conference, lecture, collaboration, and event venue
buildings.exteriorMotif: low basalt and concrete ring with four illuminated foyer wedges, one rising walkable roof, planted discussion terraces, and retractable petal canopies

buildings.name: Access and Protocol House
buildings.purpose: laboratory registration, certification, equipment authorization, and safety access
buildings.exteriorMotif: two engraved pale ceramic volumes joined by an upper bridge around a transparent gate passage with standardized status strips and credential service ports
buildings.lighting: standard cyan green amber ultraviolet access strips

buildings.name: Benchlight Laboratory Arcade
buildings.purpose: principal collection of bookable micro-laboratories
buildings.exteriorMotif: two long modular laboratory bars facing Bench Street beneath a transparent photovoltaic roof with ordered utilities, switchable windows, booking strips, and separate rear service interfaces
buildings.lighting: module vacancy preparation occupancy cleaning indicators

buildings.name: The Instrument Lantern
buildings.purpose: imaging, spectroscopy, microscopy, and precision measurement
buildings.exteriorMotif: milky channel-glass cube hovering above a vibration plinth with black grid, brass calibration lines, transparent cooling spine, freight tower, and nanometre plaza scales

buildings.name: QuickMatter Materials and Chemistry Studios
buildings.purpose: bookable coatings, polymer, electrochemistry, microfluidics, and formulation work
buildings.exteriorMotif: low repeating sawtooth bays in chemical ceramic with dark loading recesses, staggered silver exhaust towers, rain-garden front, and screened technical rear

buildings.name: BioMinute Sample Laboratories
buildings.purpose: contained low-risk sample preparation, microscopy, cell-free assays, and environmental testing
buildings.exteriorMotif: rounded triangular bioceramic complex around an isolation garden with three filtration towers, green glazing, bioswale bridges, frosted status bands, and cold-chain porch

buildings.name: Circuit Yard Electronics and Robotics Studios
buildings.purpose: electronics, sensors, small robots, drones, and hardware assembly
buildings.exteriorMotif: five folded-roof halls opening to a grid test yard with obstacles, charging pylons, motion-capture fence, overhead rails, drone pads, and copper-orange safety edges

buildings.name: DryLab 24
buildings.purpose: computational studios, simulation, visualization, remote instruments, and digital twins
buildings.exteriorMotif: slender faceted seven-storey smoked-glass tower with matte black electronic-ink fields, vertical opaline data strips, solid southern face, sunken planted plaza, and Instrument Lantern bridge
buildings.placementZone: inner scientific ring and dark-sky edge
buildings.lighting: north and east data strips only

buildings.name: Aqua Meridian Covered Pool
buildings.purpose: principal guest swimming complex and leisure landmark
buildings.exteriorMotif: flattened elliptical timber and dark-steel shell with clear, photovoltaic, and shaded panels above a sheltered stone promenade and reed rain basins

buildings.name: Blue Hour Recovery Baths
buildings.purpose: quiet warm-water recovery and wellness
buildings.exteriorMotif: low frosted cylindrical vessels wrapped in bronze rings beneath a branching glass canopy with steam vents, grasses, water channels, and winding arrival

buildings.name: Orbit Leisure Pavilion
buildings.purpose: exercise, climbing, sports, movement classes, and informal team recreation
buildings.exteriorMotif: circular glazed loop behind folded silver mesh with diagonal structure, protected climbing surfaces, rooftop running path, gradual ramps, cross-building view passages, and kinetic wind fins

buildings.name: The Perpetual Table
buildings.purpose: primary 24-hour food hall
buildings.exteriorMotif: long two-storey colonnaded hall beneath dark metal roof and irregular lanterns with controlled restaurant fronts, retractable weather walls, sculptural chimneys, and world-time plaza

buildings.name: The Greenhouse Refectory
buildings.purpose: restaurant, orchard terrace, and visible edible growing
buildings.exteriorMotif: connected glass gables with black steel, bronze vents, trees, vines, raised beds, water channels, suspended canopy, orchard terrace, and herb-wall service screen

buildings.name: Afterlight Sky Restaurant
buildings.purpose: formal restaurant and northern visual landmark
buildings.exteriorMotif: bronze glass prism cantilevered from dark stone tower above a reflecting pool with wrapping stair, glass lift, black-chrome canopy, reflective underside, and roof terrace

buildings.name: Minute Market
buildings.purpose: primary general-purpose nonstop mall
buildings.exteriorMotif: two-storey rounded opaline rectangle around a membrane-covered tree court with champagne frames, curved corners, recessed fronts, monochrome sign band, pickup wall, balcony, and four stairs

buildings.name: Null Hour Arcade Mall
buildings.purpose: dense nocturnal retail beside the Transit Lodge
buildings.exteriorMotif: five-storey wedge of black brick, steel, glass block, projecting canopies, open stairs, small upper shopfronts, sheltered automat alley, steam vents, and intermittent time sign
buildings.lighting: amber white red and pale cyan blade signs

buildings.name: Orbit Supply Court
buildings.purpose: scientific supply retail wrapped around a covered ring-transit stop
buildings.exteriorMotif: incomplete modular retail ring with five directional gaps under a broad roof, dark red steel, translucent glazing, route-map light band, transit pulses, photovoltaic terraces, collectors, and communications mast

buildings.name: The Ever Hour
buildings.purpose: flagship all-hour hotel, arrival hall, sky lobby, observatory lounge, and civic heart of the guest district
buildings.exteriorMotif: four monumental basalt and bronze-glass hotel towers around the public Continuum crossing, joined by elevated opaline sky lobbies beneath an illuminated time crown and THE EVER HOUR facade
buildings.placementZone: exact civic middle of the Ever Hour District
buildings.lighting: continuous pale-gold room bands, opaline sky lobbies, illuminated name facade, and slow astronomical crown
